# Platform Overview and Architecture

Dimension covering what Notion is, its history, block-based architecture, backend
infrastructure, pricing, and platform availability. See [citations.md](../citations.md)
for full source details.

## What Notion Is

Notion is "a single space where you can think, write, and plan. Capture thoughts,
manage projects, or even run an entire company — and do it exactly the way you
want" [1]. Wikipedia describes it as a "collaboration platform with kanban boards,
tasks, wikis and databases" for notetaking, knowledge management, data
organization, and project tracking [4]. The Markdown Guide calls it "an all-in-one
knowledge management solution" [14].

## Platform Availability

Windows, macOS, Android, iOS, and web browsers. Multiple languages including
English, French, German, Japanese, Korean, Spanish [4].

## Block-Based Architecture

Everything in Notion is a block with four attributes [2]:

1. **ID** — "each block is uniquely identifiable by its ID" using UUID v4
2. **Properties** — data structures storing custom attributes; `title` for text,
   "user-defined properties" for database pages
3. **Type** — defines rendering behavior; accessible via "/" menu
4. **Relationships** — two pointer systems:
   - **Content** — "an array (or ordered set) of block IDs" (children)
   - **Parent** — "the block ID of the block's parent" (permission inheritance)

"Indentation is structural: it's a reflection of the structure of the render
tree" [2].

"Blocks inherit permissions based on the blocks in which they're located (which
are above them in the tree)" [2].

### Client-Server Lifecycle

Operations define attribute changes, grouped into transactions. Local state
updates within milliseconds. Transactions stored in IndexedDB/SQLite via
TransactionQueue pending server confirmation [2].

Server processes via `/saveTransactions` [2]:
1. Load affected blocks ("before" state)
2. Duplicate and apply operations ("after" state)
3. Validate permissions and data coherency
4. Commit to source-of-truth database
5. Schedule background work (version history, indexing, MessageStore)

### Real-Time Sync

WebSocket connections to MessageStore for live updates. Clients subscribe to
block changes. Version mismatches trigger `syncRecordValues` API calls.
RecordCache (LRU on SQLite/IndexedDB) for local persistence [2].

## Backend Infrastructure

| Metric | Value | Year | Source |
|--------|-------|------|--------|
| Total blocks stored | 200+ billion | 2024 | [15] |
| Block rows in Postgres | ~20 billion | 2021 | [15] |
| Data growth rate | Doubles every 6-12 months | — | [15] |
| Data volume | Hundreds of terabytes (compressed) | — | [15] |
| Physical Postgres instances | 32 → 96 | 2021 → 2023 | [15] |
| Logical shards | 480 (as stated in [15]; 15 per instance in 2021, 5 per instance in 2023) | 2021-2023 | [15] |
| Data lake cost savings | $1M+ annually | 2022 | [15] |
| Ingestion latency improvement | 1+ day → minutes/hours | — | [15] |

Data lake pipeline: Debezium CDC → Kafka → Apache Hudi → S3. One connector per
Postgres host in AWS EKS. Apache Spark for transformations [15].

## Pricing (as of 2026-03-30)

| Tier | Monthly | Annual | Key Differentiators |
|------|---------|--------|---------------------|
| Free | $0 | $0 | 5MB file upload, 7-day history, 10 guests, 1 chart |
| Plus | $12/member | $10/member | Unlimited blocks/uploads/guests, 30-day history |
| Business | $24/member | $20/member | SAML SSO, 90-day history, Notion Agent, AI Meeting Notes |
| Enterprise | Custom | Custom | Unlimited history, audit logs, SCIM, zero AI data retention |

Additional: Custom domains $8–10/month each, Custom Agents $10/1,000 credits
(Beta) [3].

## AI and Additional Products

- Notion AI — content generation and database automation [1]
- Custom Agents — task automation (Beta, credit-based) [1][3]
- AI Meeting Notes — transcription and summaries [1]
- Enterprise Search — cross-app search (Beta) [1]
- Notion Calendar, Notion Mail, Notion Sites [1]
